FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 389
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Rex Reynolds
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 05/08/2023
House Bill 389 as introduced would increase receipts to the non-reverting Alabama 988 Crisis
Care Fund, created by this bill in the State Treasury to be managed by the Alabama Department
of Mental Health (ADMH), by an estimated $69 million annually by levying a $0.98 monthly
surcharge on certain communication services, as well as a similar surcharge on certain prepaid
retail transactions, beginning October 1, 2024. This bill provides that this surcharge could be
adjusted by the 988 Study Commission to an amount no more than $3 and no less than $0.98.
This bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Revenue (ADOR)
to collected these surcharges; however, these obligations would be offset, in whole or in part, by
the deduction of up to 2% of the amount of surcharges collected that would be retained by
ADOR, in an amount agreed upon by ADMH and ADOR. This bill would also provide for up to
2% of surcharges collected to be paid from the fund monthly to reimburse certain
communication services providers for the cost of collecting and remitting the surcharge.
This bill would provide for monies in this fund to be used by ADMH to fund 988 related
services and to develop, coordinate, and administer Alabama's Crisis System of Care, including
988 call centers, mobile crisis services, and crisis centers.
Further, this bill would create the 14-member Study Commission on the 988 Comprehensive
Behavioral Health Crisis Communication System to study the impact of the Crisis System of
Care and to provide oversight to the fund, which will increase the obligations of, presumably,
the 988 Crisis Care Fund by an estimated $2,500 for travel and per diem expenses for each
meeting held.
